changes: Accept owner owns all accepted connection children through JoinSet, reaps typed results and closes endpoint explicitly on owner teardown.
Connection close state includes generation and is captured before child scheduling; immediate reopen cannot erase a previous close for existing children.

Pinned serving future and later-declared connection Drop guard establish explicit QUIC zero closure before H3 server destructor sends0x100. Exact server destructor source is separately partial-read and hashed.
Cancellation surrounds incoming TLS/QUIC and the entire connected H3 future, including bootstrap, partial request resolution, rejection and nested relay awaits.

Typed background failures are retained and drainable; relay send/read errors propagate, with existing Windows ICMP reset exception. Rejection permits only exact remote application code zero as deliberate peer teardown.

Eight final real-QUIC controls establish authentication/settings or literal403/407 response barriers, keep peer endpoint/driver alive, require typed closure and actual proxy-address rebind. Duplicate critical stream requires exact protocol103 and retained typed local error.
Explicit child path is necessary because support.rs already selects the parent via a path attribute; root confirmed E0583 on both compile hosts before registration correction.

limits: No fresh runtime reproduction or gate result is claimed. Six baseline failing outcomes are forecasts for root execution.

Controls independently cover authenticated H3-ready pre-CONNECT and rejected/challenged stages. Raw stalled TLS/bootstrap and live relay UDP cancellation are covered by source ownership but not separate new runtime controls. Existing composed connect_udp paths still require root execution.
Socket rebind is a bounded ten-second observation after typed peer closure; no perpetual or cross-platform runtime conclusion before actual root runs.

Owner Drop requests asynchronous cancellation; JoinSet drops abort children and endpoint guard signals explicit QUIC closure. Completed runtime cleanup must be established by peer closure/address release controls.
Background failures remain accessible in take_failures; existing callers are not rewritten to inspect them. Their response/status/path oracles remain independently required.
No protocol parser generality, production behavior, full architecture completion, source-layout closure or audit inventory update is implied.
